The present claim is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No. 478/2016,
Police Station Shakarpur under section 279/337 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: 1 2. The accident in the present case took place in the evening of 11.03.2016.
The petitioner Yunus Khan was going to his duty from his scooter No. DL-3S-CZ-5431(Activa).
When he reached Geeta Colony, a car registration no.UP-16-AR-6466 driven in a rash and negligent manner and high speed hit his scooter from behind.
Due to the collision, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
The petitioner was taken to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital and discharged on the same day.
The petitioner has claimed Rs.4,00,000/- as compensation.

3. After completion of the investigation in the accident, the present Detail Accident Report (DAR)
was filed.
4. On notice of the petition, the respondent no. 1 & 2 filed reply.

The respondent no. 1 who is the driver & owner of the offending car has taken the defence that the accident happened due to the fault of petitioner himself as petitioner had taken a sudden wrong left turn without any indication.
5. The respondent no.2 ICICI Lombard GIC Ltd./ insurance company took the general defences.

Further, it is stated that the driver/owner of the offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol (98 mg%) and therefore the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 22.11.2016 - (i) Whether Claimant has suffered injuries in roadside accident on 11.03.2016 involving vehicle i.e. Car bearing registration No. UP-16-AR-6466 being driven allegedly in a rash and negligent manner by R-1?
(ii)Whether the Claimant is entitled for any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

(OPP)
(iii) Relief.
7. In order to establish his claim, petitioner Yunus Khan has examined himself as PW1.

ASI Anand Kumar is examined as PW2 who stated that he reached the spot of accident, took the injured to LBS Hospital, recorded statement of injured/petitioner, prepared complaint and got registered the FIR through constable Jaiveer.
He obtained the result of MLC of injured, which was simple.

Thereafter,
he filed the chargesheet under section 173 Cr.PC.

The driver Vishwanath Gupta was found under the influence of alcohol of 98% mg.
8.
Petitioner also examined Dr. Manoj Teotia as PW3.
As per evidence of PW3 Dr. Manoj Teotia, the patient Yunus Khan was examined vide MLC Mark X.
Patient sustained - abrasion over vertex red in colour, tenderness over left shoulder.
After giving first aid, the patient was referred to senior resident for detailed examination and expert opinion.
9. In his defence, the respondent no. 1 Vishwa Nath Gupta examined himself as R1W1.
According to his evidence the accident was caused due to the negligence of petitioner himself and that he was not drunk at the time of accident.

sentences.text:
Respondent no. 3/insurance company examined its Legal Executive Prakhar Singh as R3W1,
who proved the policy, Ex.R3W1/1 and proved the condition of the policy that "any accidental loss or damage suffered whilst the insured or any person driving the vehicle with the knowledge and consent of the insured is under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs shall be a violation of the condition of the policy ."
11.

The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1: Whether Claimant has suffered injuries in roadside accident on 11.03.2016 involving vehicle i.e.Car bearing registration No. UP-16AR-6466 being driven allegedly in a rash and negligent manner by R-1?
12. In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, the Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
13. Now in this case, the petitioner is the injured and witness of the accident.

In order to establish his claim, petitioner Yunus Khan has examined himself as PW-1 and proved the DAR Ex.PW1/1,
medical treatment document Ex.PW1/2, medical leave application Ex.PW1/3 and salary slip Ex.PW1/4.
He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the car which hit him from back.
He deposed that he is working as Head Constable in Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) New Delhi and getting salary of Rs.40,299/- per month.

entities.text: Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the evening of 11.03.2016, he was going to his duty, NDCCZ Building, Jai Singh Road, from his scooter No. DL-3S-CZ-5431(Activa).

When he reached Geeta Colony, a car registration no.
UP-16-AR-6466 came in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed, hit his scooter from behind.
Due to the collision, he fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
He was taken to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital.
The driver of the offending car was in inebriated condition due to consumption of liquor.
After discharge from Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital, he took further treatment from Safdarjung Hospital, where he was referred to Global Diagnostic for check-up.
He also got his treatment in Central Government health Scheme in Vasant Kunj, Delhi.
He spent about Rs.80,000/- on his treatment, Rs.20,000/- on special diet.
He joined his duty after 60 days.
He has claimed total compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-.
14. In defence, the respondent No.1 denied the allegations of the complainant and stated that it was the negligence of the petitioner which caused the accident.
1 which means that he has not denied the accident or the involvement of his vehicle but has only said that the accident occurred due to the fault of the petitioner himself.
The insurance company has not proved anything contrary to the claim of the petitioners.
15. After investigation, the police filed the chargesheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the car.
Filing of chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima faice points to his culpability.

sentences.text: 16. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of chargesheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party do not accept such chargesheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.

17. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, it is proved that petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1, the driver of the offending car.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No. 2 Whether the Claimant is entitled for any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

(OPP) 
18. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

19. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343 is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court delineating on the general principles relating to compensation in injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the basis of this judgment the compensation in this case is calculated as follows.

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
20.
Petitioner has stated in his evidence affidavit that he is working Head Constable in Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) New Delhi and has spent around Rs.80,000/- on his medical treatment.

entities.text: Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
As the petitioner is a government employee,
he was covered under the Central Government Health Scheme which he also admitted in evidence.
In cross-examination, he has admitted that he has not placed on record medical bills regarding his treatment.

He admitted that as per MLC No.
3338 dated 11.03.2016, the nature of injury was simple.
He admitted that all medial and treatment bills were reimbursed from the department under the CGHS scheme.
Under this head only the actual medical bills /expenses are reimbursed.

Accordingly,
no compensation is granted under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:

4 21.

sentences.text: As per MLC, the petitioner received simple injury and no internal injury found.
On the basis of the treatment record as well as the nature of injury I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.25,000/- to the petitioner under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
22.

Since the petitioner is a government employee and was injured on duty, therefore,
he would have not suffered any loss in his income during the period of his medical treatment or the medical leaves availed by him.
And in case he suffered some pecuniary loss then he was duty bound to show it and place that loss before the tribunal.
But he has not proved or deposed that he had suffered any loss of income by this injury during his medical leaves.
On the contrary, he admitted that his salary was not deducted for leave taken by him from the month of March 2016 to August 2016.
He further admitted that as per CGHS he got leave and all the leaves had been reimbursed by the department and nothing monetary loss has been caused to him.
In that scenario, it is not possible to grant him any compensation under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 23.

The petitioner has claimed Rs.20,000/- for special diet but he has not proved the actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.5,000/- to petitioner for special diet.

24. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarised as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1 Medical Expenses NIL  2 Pain & Sufferings Rs.25,000 /-
 3 Special diet Rs.5,000/-
 4 Conveyance & Attendant charges NIL.
 5 Loss of income during treatment NIL  TOTAL Rs.30,000/-
Issue No. 3

Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so,
at what rate and for which period?
Petitioner has pursued the case diligently.
Accordingly, petitioner shall be entitled for interest @ 7% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realisation.

LIABILITY:
26.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability Yunish Khan vs Vishwa Nath Gupta & Another on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190044844/
5 to indemnify the insured and, in this case, insurance company has been able to prove the breach of a term of insurance policy that the driver of the offending vehicle who is also its owner was under influence of liquor which was beyond the permissible limits under the Motor Vehicles Act, the company after paying the compensation shall be entitled for recovery rights from respondent no. 1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The fact that the respondent no. 1 was under the influence of liquor has been duly proved by his MLC and the evidence of the investigation officer and is considered as established on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.

RELIEF:
27.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.30,000/- (Rs Thirty Thousand only) along with interest @ 7% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of accident till realisation in favour of petitioner against the respondent insurance company.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.

28. Form IV-B in terms of MCTAP are annexed herewith as Annexure A.
